summary.text: Three candidates converge across every layer: CA9, CD70 and NNMT. Each is raised in tumour at RNA and protein in CPTAC, replicates in TCGA-KIRC, keeps its signal when extrapolated to a pure tumour, and has independent ccRCC literature behind it. CA9 leads the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and is the only gene that stays in the top 10 under random re-weighting of the overall score. CD70 follows (score 4.2143) and has clinical-stage antibodies. NNMT adds an adverse prognostic signal (TCGA Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479) that CA9 and CD70 lack.

A second tier of target candidates has strong data support but little or no literature in this corpus. SCARB1 is first in the target profile and has an Open Targets genetic association. ENPP3 has an antibody-drug conjugate (AGS-16C3F) that reached Phase 2. SLC16A3 (MCT4) is a lactate exporter tied to the Warburg-type rewiring of ccRCC. These are well-supported data candidates; their literature gap reflects a small corpus, not contrary evidence.

The biomarkers form a separate group. PSAT1 and NNMT lead the biomarker profile, and the lost proximal-tubule genes ALDOB (Cox log HR -0.358, padj 2.3e-05), SLC22A8 (Cox log HR -0.402) and ALDH6A1 track with survival when retained. None of the lost genes is a therapeutic target, because the protein is absent from the tumour cells.

No top candidate is a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines. The only partly selective dependency found is EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha; selectivity 0.3, padj 0.061), which the approved drug belzutifan already targets. MTOR is a strong dependency but is flagged as common essential. The case for CA9, CD70, SCARB1 and ENPP3 therefore rests on tumour-selective surface expression (antibody, ADC, imaging or cell-therapy delivery), not on essentiality. VHL, PBRM1 and BAP1 are the drivers behind this programme, not direct targets.

omics.text: CA9 has the strongest and most consistent tumour-up signal: RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269 in CPTAC. CD70 (RNA log2FC 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SCARB1 (RNA 2.974, protein 1.837), ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544) and SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279) show the same concordant RNA and protein gain. FABP6 is also up (RNA 4.006, protein 1.921), with a CNV gain frequency of 0.573 and a positive cis effect (rho 0.309), so copy-number gain contributes to its rise.

The largest losses are in proximal-tubule identity genes: ALDOB (RNA log2FC -7.028, protein -2.273), SLC22A8 (RNA -6.715, protein -2.264), PCK1 (RNA -4.424, protein -1.859), PSAT1 (RNA -3.867, protein -1.963) and ALDH6A1 (RNA -3.399, protein -1.925). ALDH6A1 lies in a frequently lost region (CNV loss frequency 0.355) with a positive cis dosage effect (rho 0.525), so part of its loss is copy-number driven.

VWF is up at RNA (log2FC 3.605) and protein (log2FC 1.284), but it is an endothelial gene. Higher expression goes with better survival (log HR -0.397, padj 1.97e-7), so it is better read as a vascular prognostic marker than as a tumour-cell target.

literature.text: Published ccRCC support concentrates on CA9, CD70 and NNMT. For CA9, a CA9-targeted PET study gives proof of concept for noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC (PMID:42473996). For CD70, papers describe overexpression in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression, a link to the hypoxia pathway, and CD70 single-domain antibody radiotracers (PMID:38195301, PMID:39510586). For NNMT, one study calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential target (PMID:41399267), and a separate non-ccRCC chemistry paper describes selective NNMT inhibitors (PMID:37523719). All of this is preclinical or early translational evidence.

The densest mechanistic literature is on hypoxia-driven metabolism rather than on the top-ranked targets. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is HIF-induced, raises glycolytic acidification and suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis together with LDHB (PMID:36722045, PMID:42331208, PMID:34970493). ENO2 is reported to drive glycolysis and to predict prognosis, but only from retrospective or in vitro studies (PMID:37760940, PMID:39091581). The only clinically validated target in the text is HIF-2 alpha: VHL loss stabilises it, and belzutifan is FDA-approved (PMID:42422841).

The literature and the data disagree in several places. ALDOB is called a potential immunotherapy target (PMID:40852386), but it is lost in tumour, so the data support only a biomarker role. CD70 is reported to be associated with overall survival (PMID:39510586), but this does not replicate in TCGA. MT1G is down in tumour yet high expression is linked to poor prognosis (PMID:38906969), and PFKP is up in tumour yet low expression is linked to poor survival (PMID:34321910). FCER1G and TYROBP are proposed as prognostic targets, but their bulk rise reflects immune infiltration. SCARB1 and ENPP3 have no extracted relations in this corpus.

external.text: Open Targets confirms clinical tractability for the two surface targets. CA9 has girentuximab (Phase 3) and its iodine-124 imaging form (Phase 2), and UniProt places it at the cell membrane. CD70 has cusatuzumab (Phase 2) and vorsetuzumab mafodotin (Phase 1), with antibody tractability at the advanced-clinical level, and UniProt places it at the plasma membrane. ENPP3 has the ADC AGS-16C3F (Phase 2). SCARB1 is predicted tractable but has no drugs.

The established ccRCC drug targets sit outside the data-driven top tier. EPAS1 (association score 0.4871, belzutifan approved) has a modest, partly selective dependency (mean effect -0.143, selectivity 0.3, padj 0.061). KDR (association score 0.4566) carries the approved VEGFR inhibitors axitinib, pazopanib, tivozanib and cabozantinib. MTOR (association score 0.525) is a dependency in every ccRCC line (mean effect -1.52) but is flagged common essential, a therapeutic-window risk. VHL (0.6466), PBRM1 (0.6348) and BAP1 (0.6079) have the top association scores but are loss-of-function drivers.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic. Paired by donor, tumour cells versus normal proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189, 6 donors), and the bulk RNA log2FC at purity 1 is 7.787 (SE 0.579), so the bulk signal comes from the malignant cells themselves.

MET is mainly held by tumour cells (RCC cells 0.935 of tumour transcripts). In contrast, KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CXCR4 is lymphocytic (CD8 T cells 0.563 of transcripts) and CD74 is myeloid (macrophages 0.436 of transcripts). These genes are not tumour-intrinsic: drugs against them act on the microenvironment. EPAS1 RNA sits mainly in endothelium (cpm share 0.626) and fibroblasts (0.27), with RCC cells carrying 0.051 of its transcripts. HIF-2 alpha is regulated mainly at the protein level, so this does not argue against its tumour-cell activity, but bulk EPAS1 RNA should not be read as a tumour readout.

Single-cell data were not available as cited evidence for CD70, NNMT or ALDOB. For these genes the tumour-intrinsic call rests on the purity extrapolation: CD70 keeps RNA log2FC 4.278 at purity 1 and NNMT keeps 5.256, while ALDOB stays lost (-6.302), consistent with loss of proximal-tubule identity.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, CA9-high spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.00172), with only weak macrophage enrichment (0.099). The composition-corrected RCC share of the spot signal is 0.999, consistent with CA9 marking the malignant compartment in situ.

KDR maps to the vasculature in situ: the endothelial composition-corrected share is 0.99, and high-KDR spots are enriched for endothelial (log2 0.271) and RCC (0.208) neighbours. This fits vessels running inside the tumour and places KDR with the anti-angiogenic, microenvironment targets.

structure.text: The molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) scores only rank candidate binding sites on AlphaFold models; they are not evidence that a degrader exists. KDR has the best-ranked site (score 0.841, volume 361.1 A3, 7 accessible lysines, pocket pLDDT 83.1), but it is an endothelial target. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine); it is small and shallow, and ligand-site recall is 0.5.

Among the discovery candidates, RAB42's best site scores 0.5348 but the pocket is tiny (37.4 A3). COL23A1's AlphaFold model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91), and its only pocket (volume 8.0 A3, score 0.2342) is not a credible site, so an antibody modality is more plausible.

discovery.text: Tumour track. COL23A1 is the leading first-in-class hypothesis (novelty 0.767). RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts, it is surface or secreted and antibody/protein tractable, and its highest vital-organ expression is low (3.0 nTPM in heart muscle). It replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 5.829) and is purity-robust (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88). RAB42 (novelty 0.705) is second: RCC cells hold 0.627 of transcripts, TCGA log2FC is 4.371 and purity-1 log2FC is 3.189. Neither is a dependency (COL23A1 DepMap mean effect 0.167, not selective).

Stroma track. OLFML2A (fibroblasts 0.647 of transcripts, TCGA log2FC 2.372, purity-1 log2FC 1.527) and JAG2 (endothelium 0.487 of transcripts, TCGA log2FC 1.549, purity-1 log2FC 1.061, Cox log HR -0.177) are antibody-tractable stromal hypotheses. Their off-tumour expression (OLFML2A 27.9 nTPM in colon, JAG2 12.7 nTPM in heart muscle) is a safety caveat, and both target the stroma, not the tumour cell.

Immune track. The pool here is mostly immune genes, and the purity layer decides. LILRB4 is carried by macrophages (0.933 of tumour transcripts) and drops from TCGA log2FC 3.7 to 0.508 at purity 1, so it is flagged as infiltration-driven: its bulk signal reflects macrophage abundance, not tumour-cell expression. None of the discovery candidates is a selective dependency; all remain data-ranked hypotheses.

validation.text: Independent TCGA-KIRC replication holds for every leading target: CA9 (log2FC 9.712), CD70 (7.09), NNMT (4.685), SCARB1 (3.989), ENPP3 (5.557) and SLC16A3 (3.291). The purity check strengthens CA9 (purity-1 log2FC 7.787), SCARB1 (3.762), CD70 (4.278), NNMT (5.256) and ENPP3 (5.278), whose gains survive extrapolation to a pure tumour. It weakens the macrophage genes, such as LILRB4, which shrink towards zero.

Prognosis separates the biomarkers from the targets. NNMT (Cox log HR 0.301) and PSAT1 (0.43, padj 5.66e-7) are adverse, while ALDOB (-0.358), SLC22A8 (-0.402), ALDH6A1 (-0.554, padj 9.45e-12), PCK1 (-0.415) and VWF (-0.397) are favourable when retained. CA9 and CD70 carry no TCGA prognostic signal. VHL (frequency 0.483), PBRM1 (0.362) and BAP1 (0.104) are the recurrent somatic drivers, and none of the top candidates is one. EPAS1 is the only partly selective DepMap dependency (padj 0.061). Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not assessed for these candidates, so that layer neither strengthens nor weakens them.

robustness.text: In the target profile, SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968), CA9 (0.941), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 (0.88), NNMT (0.88), ENPP3 (0.823) and FABP6 (0.803) keep a top-10 position under random re-weighting and form the robust core. In the biomarker profile only NNMT (0.973), PSAT1 (0.96) and ALDH6A1 (0.808) are robust. ALDOB, rank 2 in the overall score, has p_top10 0.493 in the biomarker profile and a very wide rank interval there.

In the overall convergence score only CA9 is robustly top 10 (p_top10 0.894, p_top25 0.983). SLC16A3, strong in the target profile, has p_top10 0.0 overall, because the mixed score dilutes its target-specific strengths. VHL ranks in the top 25 overall, but its 95th-percentile rank reaches 580, so its position comes entirely from the genetics weight. Target calls here therefore use the target profile and biomarker calls the biomarker profile.

integration.text: All layers converge on CA9: tumour-up RNA and protein, TCGA replication, purity-robust, held by RCC cells in single-cell and spatial data, a Phase 3 antibody and literature support. CD70 agrees on expression, tractability and literature, but the literature's prognostic claim does not replicate in TCGA. NNMT is the one candidate where omics, prognosis and literature align on both target and biomarker roles, although it has no clinical drug.

The layers disagree in three places. SCARB1, ENPP3 and SLC16A3 are strong in omics and external data but almost absent from the literature corpus. ALDOB is promoted in the literature as an immunotherapy target, but it is lost in tumour and should be treated as a biomarker. The validated drug targets (EPAS1, KDR, MTOR) do not reach the top of the data-driven ranking, because their tumour-cell expression change is modest or, for KDR and EPAS1 RNA, sits in the stroma. The ranking measures expression-led convergence, not clinical validation.

targets.rationale: Top of the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.941). RNA log2FC 6.312, protein log2FC 2.269, TCGA log2FC 9.712, purity-1 log2FC 7.787, and tumour cell versus proximal tubule log2FC 7.739. Girentuximab reached Phase 3, and CA9-PET has proof-of-concept data. There is no DepMap dependency, so it suits antibody delivery and imaging rather than functional inhibition.

Concordant RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (2.421) gain, TCGA log2FC 7.09, purity-1 log2FC 4.278, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.88). Cusatuzumab (Phase 2) and vorsetuzumab mafodotin (Phase 1) exist, with radiotracer literature. Listed as a target rather than a biomarker because the TCGA prognostic association is not significant (padj 0.175).

Robust in both profiles (biomarker p_top10 0.973, target 0.88). RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709, TCGA log2FC 4.685, and adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479). Supported by a ccRCC study and by selective inhibitors from another field. Placed below CD70 only because it has no clinical drug.

First in the target profile and the most stable target call (p_top10 0.968). RNA log2FC 2.974, protein log2FC 1.837, TCGA log2FC 3.989, purity-1 log2FC 3.762, with an Open Targets genetic association of 0.519. Placed below CA9, CD70 and NNMT, despite its higher target-profile score, because it has no ccRCC literature relations and no drug.

RNA log2FC 3.895, protein log2FC 1.544, TCGA log2FC 5.557, purity-1 log2FC 5.278, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823). The ADC AGS-16C3F reached Phase 2. There is no literature in this corpus.

MCT4 lactate exporter: RNA log2FC 3.435, protein log2FC 2.279, TCGA log2FC 3.291, purity-1 log2FC 3.821, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.881). It ranks low in the overall score (p_top10 0.0) only because the mixed weights dilute its target strengths; it has no extracted literature here.

Included as the clinically validated reference despite a modest expression signal. It is the only partly selective ccRCC dependency found (mean effect -0.143, selectivity 0.3, padj 0.061), and belzutifan is approved. Its RNA sits mostly in stroma in single-cell data, but its activity is regulated at the protein level downstream of VHL loss.

Top of the biomarker profile and robust (p_top10 0.96). It is down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein (-1.963), and its TCGA Cox log HR is 0.43 (padj 5.66e-7), so higher expression within tumours is adverse.

Robust in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.808). It is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (-1.925), partly through copy-number loss (CNV loss frequency 0.355, cis rho 0.525), and retained expression is favourable (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12).

Rank 2 overall (score 4.2206). It is lost in tumour (RNA log2FC -7.028, protein -2.273, TCGA -4.741), and retained expression is favourable (Cox log HR -0.358, padj 2.3e-05). Placed below PSAT1 and ALDH6A1 because its biomarker-profile position depends on the weights (p_top10 0.493). The literature's immunotherapy-target label is not supported.

Proximal-tubule transporter lost in tumour (RNA log2FC -6.715, protein -2.264, TCGA -6.154); retained expression is favourable (Cox log HR -0.402). Rank 4 overall (score 4.1667). It marks loss of tubule identity and is not a target.

limitations.text: Bulk CPTAC cohort of modest size (110 tumours); immune and stromal genes partly reflect infiltration, which the purity extrapolation only partly corrects.
No top candidate is a selective DepMap dependency; target calls for surface proteins rest on expression selectivity, not essentiality.

The literature corpus is small (about 320 abstracts) and many biomarker relations come from single bioinformatic studies, so missing literature for SCARB1, ENPP3 or SLC16A3 is a gap, not negative evidence.
TCGA survival associations are univariate and not adjusted for stage or grade.

Two cell-agent findings (a CA9 single-cell summary and the GAL3ST4 immune-track candidate) failed numeric verification and are not reported; single-cell evidence for CD70, NNMT and ALDOB was not available, and EGFR was not queried.
The phosphosite and kinase-activity layers were not explored by the omics agent, and STRING interactions were not examined.
MGD scores rank predicted pockets on AlphaFold models only; they do not imply that a degrader exists or can be made.
Single-cell and spatial results rest on 12 donors, and the tumour-versus-proximal-tubule test on 6.
